column3: Re-arm the air attack until the next move starts: the HAR may attack again in the air (add jj to chain mid-move)
Ignore the side walls on this frame; on a spawned object one frame turns off its edge and floor handling for good
Turn to face the middle of the arena this frame; the facing stays until the robot next turns toward the opponent
Turn around if the player holds back; held back flips every tick of a multi-tick frame, so keep ad frames one tick long
Launched object just disappears when its animation ends, skipping the follow-up animation its move names
A landing hit freezes the opponent for damage-value ticks instead of hurting it; its next hit taken releases it
On a jump-category move, the opponent may block this frame holding forward as well as back; repeat on every frame
A hit lands as a launcher: a grounded opponent flies up and back. Read one tick late, so tag the frame before too
Walk to a point set by e (opponent), cf, g, x+/y+ on the frame; the frame holds until the HAR arrives. Pair with bm10
Launched object bounces off the screen sides and settles on the floor; with no follow-up move it jumps to tick 25
Object flies a looping path over the upper screen, ignoring its speed and gravity; put on every frame (fire-pit orbs)
Teleport sideways: held left/right picks a random spot by that wall, else 40 px behind the opponent (Chronos)
Hitting a side wall starts the move's follow-up (as if it connected); in the air, also keeps sideways speed at the wall
Ignore the floor: a falling HAR drops through it without landing, so the move goes on; repeat on every frame
Turn the robot around. Repeats every tick the frame shows, so use a 1-tick frame. ear: face the opponent's way.
Acts as at (teleport), cancels a* tags written before it on the frame and turns earlier u* tags into a* tags. Use at
No effect: a b with no recognised second letter is ignored as if deleted; the next character keeps its meaning
At round end, start a new match vs secret FIRE (from FIRE: ICE). One/two-player only; use on Fire Pit-only moves.
Fire Pit secret only: break the floor grate, showing a burning hole and stopping all scrap for the rest of the match
Vertical screen shake of magnitude N, decaying one step per cycle; sign picks the first direction
Hold the round-end countdown at 30 while this frame plays (scrap / destruction / victory cinematics)
Dissolve threshold for the sprite this frame: 255 = all pixels drawn, lower = fewer; with bs it fades over the frame
Move by the authored x/y amounts this frame, skipping the pilot agility scaling
Horizontal screen shake of magnitude N, decaying each cycle; sign picks the first direction
Overlay animation N: parsed every tick after the main animation and drawn instead of it, until bx
Switch immediately to animation N: frame counter 0, hit state cleared, N's first frame parsed this tick
Dissolve start value: with bf, fades the dissolve from N to the bf value over this frame
Move the HAR toward the arena centre (x = 160): slides while a v tag is active, otherwise snaps
Spawned object casts a floor shadow (sets the blend-render bit)
Stop the bm overlay animation
Palette index whose colour the standard blend path fades toward (0 = black)
Start palette index for the standard blend path
Palette entry count for the standard blend path; also enables the per-frame blend fade
Standard palette blend range = this player's own HAR colour slots (1-47 for P1, 48-95 for P2)
Blend level at the end of this frame (0 = palette untouched, 64 = fully at the target colour); with bpb and bpn in the same frame, fades from bpb to bpp
Blend level at the start of this frame's fade; needs bpp and bpn in the same frame
Use the palette-remap blend path (bi/bc/ba/bd) this frame instead of the standard bps/bpn/bpd blend
Standard palette blend uses the luminance-weighted formula this frame instead of the plain lerp
Palette remap: number of gradient groups written after the source group, one per bd target
Palette remap: colours per group; also the per-pixel palette step for bg sprites
Palette remap: take the RGB fade targets from this animation's last frame (3 bytes per group, after a 3-byte header)
Draw the sprite as a brightness map: each pixel value shifts the screen pixel's palette index by that many bc-sized groups
Palette remap: first palette index of the source colour group
Unused: jump to the end of the animation unless the opponent is in animation N and no spawn is playing it
Unblockable contact frame: a back-holding opponent is hit anyway (a real block animation still blocks)
Shadow offset: shift the spawned object's shadow N pixels; bo0 (or bare bo) turns the shadow off this frame
Draw the sprite additively over the background (energy / glow effects)
Draw the sprite as a darkened translucent ghost (also applied automatically while in stasis)
Turn the shadow off this frame (same as bo0)
With am: walk to the far corner from the opponent instead of to the opponent, and face inward on arrival (Shadow scrap)
Defer the frame's d<N> seek until the HAR next lands (negative N counts from the animation's end)
When this animation ends on the ground, chain into its play-if-hit animation instead of returning to idle (the tag must be on the final frame)
Hit pause: when this frame's attack connects or is blocked, stall the fight for the Options hit-pause time (once per animation)
Arm a wall trigger on the opponent: when the HAR itself reaches a side wall, the opponent switches to the animation loaded by jn
Player steering: add N x 0.1 x held-direction x agility to the horizontal speed each frame (HARs and spawns)
Player steering on the Y axis for spawned objects; on the HAR itself the engine reads the d value instead, so it has no effect there
Re-enter animation at N ticks.  If negative, enter animation this many ticks from the end
Snap to the opponent's position and facing (with am: walk there instead); a spawned object snaps to its owner's opponent
Flip the sprite vertically this frame (toggle; spawns inherit it)
Snap to the floor: Y to ground level, vertical speed 0, on-ground set
Zero the horizontal and vertical speed this frame (spawns also drop their cx/cy steering)
If this attack is blocked, the attacker switches to the move's play-if-hit animation
Allow chaining into a destruction move from this frame
Allow chaining into a scrap move from this frame
Allow chaining into a close-range (throw) move from this frame
Allow chaining into a high move from this frame
Allow chaining into a jumping move from this frame
Allow chaining into a low move from this frame
Allow chaining into a medium move from this frame
Allow chaining into a projectile move from this frame
Allow chaining into any move category from this frame
Allow chaining into animation N specifically from this frame; also the target cw switches to
Damage weight for this frame's hit: the opponent takes (N+10) percent of the move's damage and stun (default 100)
Volume for sounds started this frame, 0-63 (sticky until the next l)
Launch angle in degrees for this frame's m12 hit debris (1000 = random); default is the fixed fan
Spawned object counts as a live hazard: floor-aware, can hit the HARs, visible to the AI, cleared at round end
Destroy every spawned object playing animation N
Gravity for the spawned object (N x 0.01 x 256 per tick on its Y speed); default 0
Particle count for this frame's m12 hit debris: N+1 pieces (default 1)
Select animation N as the target of mo / mu in this parse round
Render layer of the spawned object, 0-63 (default 27; fighters draw at 30/31). No effect from a BK scene animation
Mark the mm-selected animation so its mu countdown pauses while the opponent is in stasis (on the opponent's copy if hit)
Spawn priority 0-15 (slot stealing, draw order); 100/101 also remove existing copies; -1 in BK strings = palette fill
Spawn X for this frame's m: random in [N, 320-N-1]
Spawn Y for this frame's m: random in [N, 200-N-1]
Spawn Y for this frame's m from the parser's current Y: (y - 188) x -4
Make the mm-selected animation unavailable for N ticks (counts down once the string stops refreshing it)
Spawn X offset for this frame's m, relative to the spawner and mirrored by facing (absolute X from a BK scene animation)
Spawn Y offset for this frame's m, relative to the spawner (absolute Y from a BK scene animation)
Spawn animation N as an object; from a HAR or spawn string relative to the spawner (+mx,my), from a BK scene animation at absolute (mx,my)
No hit detection for this frame (also marks spawned objects as non-colliding)
Draw the sprite N pixels forward of its position this frame (mirrored by facing); spawns made this frame inherit it
Draw the sprite N pixels down from its position this frame (negative = up); also shifts the shadow base
HAR palette effect: use the luminance-weighted blend formula instead of the plain lerp
HAR palette effect: blend level at the start of the fade-in (0-511)
HAR palette effect: blend level at the end of the fade-out (0-511)
Start a HAR palette effect toward palette colour N: fade in over ptd ticks to pp, hold ptp ticks, fade out over ptr ticks to pc
Following p tags in this frame apply to the opponent HAR instead
Ignore the p tags of this parse unless the target HAR is in its damage animation
HAR palette effect: peak blend level (0-511); also resets pb and pc
Replace the whole VGA palette with the animation's last frame data
HAR palette effect: fade-in duration in ticks (0-127)
HAR palette effect: peak hold duration in ticks (0-127)
HAR palette effect: fade-out duration in ticks (0-127)
Multi-hit counter: hit number N (1-15) may connect once; repeat on each frame; q1 re-opens the hit every frame
Flip the sprite horizontally this frame (toggle; spawns inherit it)
Play sound N this frame: 0-49 from the HAR's own sound table, 50+ from the arena / other HAR tables
This frame's sound keeps panning to follow the HAR while it plays
Stereo pan start for this frame's sound (-128..127); without it the pan comes from the position
Force this frame's sound onto channel N (1-3; 4 wraps to 1); sc0 = auto channel, stopping a copy already playing
Skip this frame's sound if the same sample is already playing
Stereo pan end for a BK-side sound: the pan sweeps from sb to se over the sample
Pitch shift for this frame's sound: -2 percent per unit below 0, +3 percent per unit above (-20..127)
Stereo pan end written raw (no +1 encoding); se is the conventional form
Stop music track N (BK strings only)
Play music track N (BK strings only)
Priority of this frame's sound (default 10): decides which busy channel it may take
Raise the hit-pause timer to N; shipped values 20-50 only decay, only 100 would freeze the fight
Play this frame's sound only if the opponent is being hit, blocking or in stasis
Draw the HAR in front (render layer 60) this frame
Spawned object forces the opponent into its damage animation, replaced by the object's own string
Spawn a fading afterimage ghost of the HAR this frame (motion blur)
Mark this HAR as a sync target this frame (read by the opponent's uf)
Spawned object is destroyed by the owner's next hit-check sweep (pilot_info bit 2)
Hit test replaced: connects at any range if the opponent is grounded and not in hit-stun; cannot be blocked (shockwave)
Fast-forward the opponent's animation to its end if they carry the uc marker
Landing this frame does not switch the HAR to the on-ground state
Before this frame's hit test the opponent loses its z immunities and becomes hittable
Set a sticky marker on the opponent that the AI's move selection reads
This frame's hit bypasses the opponent's hit gate (marker on the opponent's direction byte)
A cornered opponent who blocks or takes this hit does not push its owner back; put on every contact frame (projectiles)
While a blocking opponent is still touched after the hit, restart their block stun every frame (holds them in block)
In a scrap or destruction move, marks the opponent scrapped (destroyed too) for the round; destruction needs the mark
Launched object ends, or switches to its follow-up, each time its owner's attacks reach the opponent
x/y on this frame set the speed (both reset first) instead of moving; held every tick, kept after the frame
Same as v: x/y set the speed instead of moving. The x is part of the tag, so a move written after vsx is lost; use vx
Same as v: x/y set the speed instead of moving; any letter after vs is swallowed, so never write v right before s
Draw behind: fighter behind its opponent this frame; launched object to the back until a later mn; arena anim at back
Move backward N pixels every tick of this frame (AGILITY-scaled on robots); with v, set the backward speed to N instead
Move forward N pixels every tick of this frame (AGILITY-scaled on robots); with v, set the forward speed to N instead
X keyframe: set X to N, slide to the next x= value by the start of its frame. Background anims only; x=0 can't slide
Horizontal scale in percent; has no visible effect, sprites always draw at full width (use y for height)
Move up N pixels every tick of this frame (AGILITY-scaled on robots); with v, set the upward speed to N instead
Move down N pixels every tick of this frame (AGILITY-scaled on robots); with v, set the downward speed to N instead
Y keyframe: set Y to N, slide to the next y= value by the start of its frame. Background anims only; y=0 can't slide
Squash or stretch the sprite vertically this frame, in percent (0-255, default 100); width and shadow stay unchanged
Close-range (throw) immunity this frame, but throws bypass it and still land; use zz to avoid being thrown
Immune to high-category attacks this frame (incl. Shadow's high copies): they pass through, no damage, no block
Immune to jumping attacks (incl. air grabs) for this frame; they pass through. Starts a tick late, lasts a tick over.
Immune to low-category attacks this frame (crouching kicks, Shadow's low copies): they pass through, no damage, no block
Immune to medium-category attacks this frame: they pass through, no damage, no block
Immune to projectile hits this frame: projectiles pass through and keep flying
Invulnerable this frame: every attack, projectile and hazard misses, nothing is blocked and no throw can start
